subject: Pricing: co-term transition & mid-contract top-up mechanics
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma.li@orionhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orionhealth.com, Amit Rao <amit.rao@orionhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 14:08:00 -0800
Subject: Pricing and co-term options for upcoming renewal

Hi Neha,

Quick context — our fiscal year shifted and the renewal window for our main account now lands in March. We launched a product pilot this summer and usage has accelerated; procurement is asking for options to either: (A) top up capacity mid-contract and pro-rate until the new March co-term, or (B) annualize early and move the whole contract to a March cycle.

Attached is a small export of our Q3 usage for the feature (Orion_Q3_usage.csv). Two asks: can you outline the practical options you support (pricing mechanics, pro-rates, voucher vs true-up, and timeline to get an amendment in place)? Also, who on your side should we expect to work with for PO/legal timing?

Ideally we’d have a short call this week to scope required paperwork.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Li
Head of Platform Product
OrionHealth

Attachments: Orion_Q3_usage.csv (CSV, 24KB)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@orionhealth.com>
Cc: procurement@orionhealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pricing and co-term options for upcoming renewal

Hi Emma — thanks for the usage file, this is helpful. Short answer: we commonly support both flows you describe. High level: 1) mid-contract top-up: immediate add-on commit or voucher with prorated billing to your next co-term; 2) early annualize: convert to a 12-month commit with a blended rate that can include a one-time credit for unused months.

Before I sketch scenarios I need two small clarifications:
- Is the ask a one-time burst (temporary) or a sustained uplift you expect to use for the next 6–12 months?
- Do you need invoicing to align to your March fiscal cadence (yes/no)?

If you’re available I can do a 30-min call Wednesday to run three priced scenarios (true-up top-up, voucher + prorate, early-annualize with credit). If that works I’ll also loop in Jordan for pricing authority and Stephanie from legal for amendment timing.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, procurement@orionhealth.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 12:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pricing: co-term transition & mid-contract top-up mechanics

Thanks Emma — looping in Jordan (pricing lead) and Stephanie (legal) for the Wed 2pm PT call. To make the discussion concrete, I sketched three scenarios below based on the usage pattern you shared. These are illustrative and will be refined on the call.

SCENARIO A — Mid-contract top-up (temporary voucher, prorated)
- Add 150k monthly token voucher for 6 months (applies immediately).
- Billing: one-time invoice for voucher purchase; partial month prorate if added mid-cycle.
- No change to existing contract end date; voucher expires at co-term.
- Expected unit price: current list — no long-term discount; volume pricing applies only to sustained commit.

SCENARIO B — Mid-contract top-up converted to committed units (annualize at co-term)
- Immediate top-up with option to convert unused portion into committed units at co-term with a blended discount.
- If converted to 12-month commit at co-term, we propose a 7% blended discount on the refreshed commit (requires 12‑month minimum).
- Billing: upfront for top-up, then rebalanced at conversion.

SCENARIO C — Early annualize (move to March cycle now)
- Move the contract to a new 12-month term starting now aligned to March; provide a credit for unused months on current term.
- Price: 10% discount on the new committed baseline if signed within 10 business days (exec-approved promotional concession).
- Legal: would require an amendment + SOW and a small schedule to process PO + PO number.

Key notes / trade-offs
- If you prioritize short-term cash predictability and minimal legal work, Scenario A is fastest (voucher + prorate).
- If you want lower unit economics long-term and are comfortable amending the term, Scenario C yields the best blended price.
- We can offer an intermediate (Scenario B) to let you trial and convert at co-term with a guaranteed floor discount.

Action items for the call (Wed 2:00pm PT):
- Confirm which scenario you prefer to explore in detail.
- Procurement: share PO cadence and any contract signoff constraints (e.g., required SOW fields).
- Redwood: we’ll prepare a one‑page commercial term sheet and a draft amendment/SOW to move quickly after the call.

I’ve attached a short example amendment template we use as a base. Jordan — any immediate adjustments you’d make to the discount levels above before the call? Stephanie — ballpark timeline for a simple amendment + SOW?

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOW-OrionHealth-draft.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Emma Li <emma.li@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, procurement@orionhealth.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pricing: co-term transition & mid-contract top-up mechanics

Thanks — reviewed the scenarios Neha put forward. Recommendation: go with Scenario B (top-up now with conversion option) for two reasons: lower immediate friction for procurement, and it gives Orion an out while guaranteeing Redwood a near-term uplift. Quick commercial decisioning notes:
- We can approve a 7% blended discount on conversion into a 12-month commit (as noted).
- If Orion signs the conversion within 45 days of co-term, we’ll lock the 7% discount and add a one-time onboarding credit of $5k to offset legal integration/testing costs.

Stephanie — legal will be able to turn the amendment + SOW in ~5 business days once we have the chosen scenario and the PO number. Emma/procurement — when you’re ready please send the PO number and any invoicing instructions so we can prepare the one-time invoice for the top-up.

Neha — I’ll draft the short term sheet and send it after the call; please include the usage baseline and expected growth assumptions from Orion’s CSV so we can price the conversion floor correctly.

Jordan Blake
Head of Sales Strategy, Redwood Inference
